Sachs's play was clearly suggested by the story of a woman who picked up what she claimed was a Jackson Pollock for five bucks in a California thrift store.
If that performance was as powerful as this I’m sorry I missed it and you shouldn’t miss her latest London appearance either.
Nobody does boozed-up raucousness like Kathleen Turner, returning to the London stage nine years after playing a definitive Martha in Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?.
But “Hotel” comes across as so much over-adrenalized hot air.

cn.t: Turner delivers a commanding performance in this two-hander about art authentication, but the play itself feels compressed and glib, mining similar territory to "Art" without digging as deep into its aesthetic questions.
